extracted.intended_audience: Applicants for an NIH NIAID K08 Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award (PA-20-203); mentored clinician-scientists preparing an NIH career-development application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation of a mentored K08 (Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development Award) application including research aims, career development/training plan, institutional commitment, vertebrate animal protocol, resource sharing, and authentication of reagents. The sample is for an NIAID/NIH K08 application (PA-20-203).

rubrics_metrics.name: Application format and FOA instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample cautions that formats/rules change over time and that applicants should follow the current FOA. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required application components (table of contents items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all standard application sections listed in the Table of Contents: SF424 R&R Cover Page; Table of Contents; Performance Sites; Research & Related Other Project Information; Project Summary/Abstract (Description); Project Narrative; Bibliography & References Cited; Facilities & Other Resources; Equipment; Research & Related Senior/Key Person; Research & Related Budget (Years 1–5); Budget Justification; PHS398 Cover Page Supplement; PHS 398 Career Development Award sections (Introduction to Application; Candidate Information and Goals for Career Development; Specific Aims; Research Strategy; Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research; Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s); Letters of Support; Description of Institutional Environment; Institutional Commitment; PHS Human Subjects and Clinical Trials Information; Vertebrate Animals; Select Agent Research; Resource Sharing; Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the order and include each listed attachment and section. The Table of Contents in the sample enumerates page locations for each required component—use it to ensure completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract and Public Health Relevance statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a concise Project Summary/Abstract describing aims, innovation, approach, and training goals, and a Public Health Relevance Statement explaining significance to public health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample gives an abstract summarizing central hypothesis, significance (reduction in transplant rejection), methods (NEVLP rat model), and career-development elements. The public-health statement should state how the work will reduce reliance on harmful drugs and its broader impact on organ transplantation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific Aims
rubrics_metrics.description: State clear, testable Specific Aims for the proposed research (the sample lists two aims: 1) Determine the dominant regulatory function of liver-resident DCregs after NEVLP; 2) Measure the impact of expanded liver-resident DCregs generated by combination cytokine therapy during NEVLP on liver graft rejection in vitro and in vivo).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aims should be concise, feasible within the project period, and aligned with the central hypothesis. Each aim should be framed so success/failure can be evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate career development and training plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the mentored career-development plan and the applicant's training goals and competencies to be developed (e.g., transplant immunology, communication, biostatistics, ethical research design).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample emphasizes protected time (applicant given protected time to devote 75% effort), assembly of an outstanding mentorship team, and concrete training goals that enable transition to research independence as a surgeon-scientist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor and co-mentor plans and qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Plans and Statements of Mentor and Co-Mentor(s) documenting mentoring roles, qualifications, and commitment (sample lists multiple named mentors and their roles).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mentor letters should describe mentoring plans, the mentor's experience training comparable candidates, and the specific support they will provide; mentors may be listed in Senior/Key Personnel with role category 'Other (Specify)-Mentor'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional commitment and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate institutional environment and commitment to the candidate's career development (e.g., protected time, start-up funds, adjacent labs, departmental support, access to research centers such as ICTR/CTSA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample documents UW-Madison and UWSMPH resources, start-up funding, protected effort (75%), adjacency of collaborators' labs, and departmental administrative and research support—these items should show an environment conducive to success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources and Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe physical resources, libraries, IT/data centers, clinical volume and hospital systems, laboratory space, cores, and relevant equipment available to support the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample describes UW libraries, Division of Information Technology, WIMR, UW Health clinical system, Department of Surgery research space, and computing hardware/software infrastructure. Detail access, security, and any shared cores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to statistical/biostatistics support
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify availability of statistical analysis and research programming resources (the Department of Surgery Statistical Analysis/Research Programming Core provides study design assistance, power analysis, analytic methods, database management, and manuscript support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe the statistical methods to be used, who will perform analyses, and access to statisticians for study design, power/sample-size calculations, and interpretation; include named cores and their capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Power calculations and sample size justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide power calculations and numerical justification for sample sizes (sample: 'Our power calculations indicate that 9 animals will be required for each experimental group in aim 1, and 9 animals... Therefore, we will require 350 animals... assuming a 10% technical failure rate, a total of 400 animals will be required').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include assumptions, effect sizes, expected variance, technical failure rates, group sizes, and total animal numbers; make statistical assumptions explicit and justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals — species and model justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify choice of animal species and model (sample: rationale for using rat orthotopic liver transplantation model and selected strains, noting similarity to human biology, cost, and laboratory expertise).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why alternatives (e.g., in vitro, computational, larger animals) are not sufficient, and why the chosen species/model is appropriate for the scientific question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals — detailed procedures and anesthesia/surgical methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide detailed description of animal procedures (donor hepatectomy, normothermic perfusion, orthotopic liver transplantation techniques, vascular cuff placement, anesthesia protocols).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include step-by-step surgical description, anesthesia agents and concentrations (e.g., isoflurane induction/maintenance), instruments, and perioperative care so IACUC reviewers can evaluate technical aspects and animal welfare.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate animals — pain minimization, perioperative care, and euthanasia
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe measures to minimize pain/distress (analgesia with buprenorphine, meloxicam as needed), daily monitoring, humane endpoints, and euthanasia methods (CO2 inhalation per AVMA guidance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State analgesic regimen, monitoring frequency, criteria for euthanasia, and adherence to AVMA and institutional policies; describe post-op care and any supportive measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal housing, veterinary oversight, and accreditation
rubrics_metrics.description: Document animal housing facilities, veterinary care and supervision, and institutional accreditation (sample: AALAC-accredited facilities, full-time board-certified veterinarians, Lab Animal Resources oversight).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide facility names, accreditation status, veterinary staff availability, and institutional oversight committees (e.g., Research Animal Resources Committee).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of relevant biological variables and experiment controls
rubrics_metrics.description: Account for biological variables (sample: gender randomly assigned for donors and recipients; use of 10–12 week old rats; co-housing to control microbiome; standardized light/diet/environment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify sex as a biological variable, age ranges, randomization procedures, housing/co-housing to control microbiome, and other measures to reduce biological confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: IACUC/ethical approvals and compliance status
rubrics_metrics.description: State IACUC review status (sample shows 'IACUC review Pending') and provide Animal Welfare Assurance numbers and approval dates when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must include IACUC approval or pending status with plan to obtain approvals prior to initiating animal work and must reference institutional assurance numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects protections and IRB status (if applicable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Declare whether human subjects/specimens/data are involved and provide IRB status/exemptions (sample: 'Are Human Subjects Involved? No' and fields for exemption numbers and IRB approval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If human subjects are involved, include IRB approval or exemption justification, Human Subject Assurance Number, and details of protections and consent procedures; if no human subjects, explicitly state so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource sharing and dissemination plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe plans to share results and resources: presentations at national meetings (e.g., American Transplant Congress), intramural seminars, peer-reviewed publications, deposit of final accepted manuscripts into PubMed Central, and open-access options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify number/target of presentations, timeline for publication, data-sharing repositories if applicable, and commitment to NIH Public Access Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of key biological and chemical resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe procedures for authenticating key reagents and resources (use of authentic suppliers, testing collagenase activity per lot, antibody titration for lot variability, media sterility and pH testing, HPLC for media supplements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List suppliers and catalog numbers, state per-lot testing plans (e.g., collagenase activity test), describe how antibodies and cytokines will be validated (titrations, activity assays), and indicate plans to document and report authentication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data security, computing infrastructure, and HIPAA compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Document computing infrastructure, physical and logical security (secure data center, next-generation firewall, off-site secure storage, access control lists, auditing, HIPAA-compliant accounts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe who has physical access, logging/auditing capabilities, password/account policies, and remote access mechanisms; explain how sensitive data will be protected in compliance with HIPAA and institutional requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory, environmental, and select-agent considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Address regulatory questions such as environmental impact, select-agent research, and historic-place designation; sample explicitly states 'This proposal does not use Select Agents for research.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete required agency questions about environmental impact assessments (EA/EIS), select-agent use, international activities, and historic-site implications; provide explanations where applicable and required authorizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications, assurances, authorized signatures, and SF424 administrative completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete SF424 (R&R) fields, certifications and assurances, authorized institutional representative signature/date, applicant organization identifiers (DUNS, EIN), contact information, and submission type (new/resubmission/continuation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional official signs where required, supply organizational identifiers, indicate resubmission status (sample: 'Resubmission'), and include cover letter and any required attachments (e.g., SFLLL, cover letter file).

rubrics_metrics.name: Project timeline, performance site identification, and congressional district
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide proposed project start and end dates, primary project/performance site location, and congressional district information (sample: Start 09/01/2021 End 08/31/2026, primary location: UW-Madison, WI-002).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include performance site addresses, congressional district codes, and tracking numbers to facilitate administrative processing; align timeline with aims and milestones.
